question.text: Two <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> long, straight wires, each carrying a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> are kept parallel to each other. If each wire experienced a force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, then separation between the wires is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
Given: F=10-5 N

Force between wires Fl=μ0i1i22πd, where, d is separation between them.

 ⇒10-50.1=2×10-7×25d

⇒d=50×10-3 m=5 cm
